extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and legal counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing approval of an affidavit of resignation (exclusion on consent) by a registered patent practitioner before the USPTO, including the kinds of misconduct alleged, the regulatory provisions implicated, and post-order obligations (publication, notice, reinstatement consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 — Affidavit of Resignation / Exclusion on Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit of Resignation submitted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 for the purpose of being excluded on consent from practice before the Office; must be approved by the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledges (inter alia) that: consent is knowingly, freely and voluntarily rendered; he is aware a disciplinary complaint is pending and of its allegations; he does not admit the allegations but understands consequences of consenting to exclusion; he understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60; he consents to being excluded from practice in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters. The Director determined the Affidavit complies with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) and approved it.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — Misleading communications / false statements to clients and Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on conduct involving false or misleading statements in the practice of patent law, including failing to inform clients of the complete and accurate status of applications, providing misleading explanations, misinforming about filings, and implying filings occurred when they did not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples alleged: (i) failing to inform a client of complete/accurate status and providing misleading explanations ('apparently there was some mixup with the correspondence'); (ii) misinforming a client about whether original paperwork could be located; (iii) stating 'Everything is in the works at the Patent Office' when not accurate; (iv) sending an $810 invoice and cashing payment knowing the work was not performed; (v) falsely implying documents had been filed when they had not. This regulation is cited in multiple client contexts in the complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — False certifications in filed papers / failure to return funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on filing papers containing false certifications and obligations to handle client funds properly (e.g., returning surplus funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include signing papers filed in the Office containing certifications pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.18 that were false, and failing to return $83 in surplus funds to a client.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — False representations in petitions to the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on falsely representing facts in petitions to revive or other submissions (e.g., representing that delay was unintentional when not true).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation: falsely representing in a petition to revive that 'The entire delay in filing the required reply ... was unintentional.'

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) — Filing/altering declarations and false certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on filing declarations or papers that are not genuine or that the practitioner knows to be false, including altering or adding pages to declarations and filing them as clients' declarations when attestations were not made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include adding the first page of a three-page declaration and filing it as the client's declaration while knowing the client had not made the required attestations, and signing papers containing false certifications under 37 C.F.R. § 11.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — Aggregate misconduct (catch-all)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on engaging in conduct described in the other listed subparagraphs (i.e., aggregative basis for discipline where multiple rule violations are involved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office alleges the respondent engaged in conduct described in subparagraphs a through f and h through k (i.e., the listed specific misconduct items), supporting a charge under § 10.23(b)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(b) — Duties in filing petitions to revive and related investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation to properly prepare and investigate petitions to the Office (e.g., petitions to revive), to file complete forms, and to investigate the truth of factual assertions before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations: filing a petition to revive that was dismissed; sending only part of a three-page USPTO form to a client for execution; filing a petition without adequately investigating whether the entire delay was unintentional; signing or permitting signature of a declaration without adequately investigating whether the representations were false.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — Communication and timeliness obligations to clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Duty to respond timely to client requests and to communicate adequately about their patent applications, and duty to act timely in filing applications and other required papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include not responding timely to clients' requests for information, failing to communicate timely and/or adequately (including not informing clients of Office communications in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(8)), not filing an application timely after being paid, and allowing client applications to become abandoned without consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a) — Duty to seek lawful objectives and carry out contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation to seek clients' lawful objectives through reasonably available means permitted by law and the Disciplinary Rules, and to carry out contracts of employment for professional services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations: failing to carry out contracts (e.g., not competently prosecuting patent applications; not timely filing after payment; not filing a petition to make special), and prejudicing or damaging clients' intellectual property rights during the professional relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.85(a)(6) — False or misleading declarations under penalty of perjury
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on signing declarations under penalty of perjury (or permitting others to sign in the practitioner's name) when those declarations contain misrepresentations about material facts (e.g., receipt of Office actions, reasons for delay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include either signing a declaration under penalty of perjury or knowingly permitting litigation counsel to sign his name to a declaration that contained misrepresentations such as: (i) the USPTO mailed a February 2, 2004 non-final Office Action to the wrong address; (ii) he never received that Office Action; and (iii) the delay in filing the required reply was unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's presumptions on reinstatement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60 implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a practitioner consents to exclusion, the OED Director will, for the limited purpose of any future reinstatement application, conclusively presume that the allegations in the pending disciplinary complaint are true and that the practitioner could not have successfully defended against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledges this presumption in his affidavit: 'if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume ... (i) the allegations ... are true; and (ii) he could not have successfully defended himself against such allegations.' This affects future reinstatement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 — Obligation to comply with conditions of exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the excluded practitioner comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as a condition of exclusion on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.' The order does not restate § 11.58's text but makes compliance a mandatory post-order obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 — Notice, publication, and reporting of public discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that the OED Director give notice of public discipline and reasons for discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in States of admission, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public, and to publish the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires publication in the OED Reading Room and the Official Gazette and directs the OED Director to 'give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies ... to courts ... and the public.' The Order cites § 11.59 as authority for these steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirements (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order will be published by the OED Director in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and notice will be published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order items: (3) OED Director shall publish this Final Order at the OED Reading Room URL; (4) OED Director shall publish the specified notice in the Official Gazette as shown in the Final Order's text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural disposition of pending disciplinary complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to dismiss the pending disciplinary complaint after acceptance of the affidavit of resignation and entry of the exclusion-on-consent order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs: 'The OED Director shall move to dismiss the pending disciplinary complaint within fourteen (14) days of the date of this Final Order.' This is a mandatory procedural step following approval of the affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall bear its own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states: 'The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.' This sets the financial consequence for the resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/Regulatory authority for order (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27 and 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's authority to approve an affidavit of resignation and exclude a practitioner on consent is grounded in statutory and regulatory provisions cited in the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes it is taken 'pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27 and 11.59,' establishing the legal basis for approving resignations and imposing public discipline and notice obligations.
